items.explanation: “churn out” = to produce large quantities of something quickly, often of low quality. Full sentence: Some websites churn out dozens of poorly researched articles a day just to attract clicks.

items.question:
Choose the correct phrasal verb:
Bargain hunters were queuing early to ___ discounted electronics.
items.explanation: “snap up” = to buy or take something quickly because it is cheap or popular. Full sentence: Bargain hunters were queuing early to snap up discounted electronics.

items.question:
Choose the correct phrasal verb:
You might want to ___ your criticism – the client is quite sensitive.
items.explanation: “tone down” = to make something less extreme, offensive or intense. Full sentence: You might want to tone down your criticism – the client is quite sensitive.

items.question:
Choose the correct phrasal verb:
The price looks cheap, but you need to ___ delivery charges and taxes.
items.meaningVi: tính đến, đưa vào tính toán
items.explanation: “factor in” = to include something when you are calculating or planning. Full sentence: The price looks cheap, but you need to factor in delivery charges and taxes.

items.question:
Choose the correct phrasal verb:
It takes courage to ___ a mistake in front of your colleagues.
items.explanation: “own up to” = to admit that you have done something wrong. Full sentence: It takes courage to own up to a mistake in front of your colleagues.

items.question:
Choose the correct phrasal verb:
Without strong leadership, the campaign is likely to ___ within months.
items.explanation: “fizzle out” = to gradually end in a weak or disappointing way. Full sentence: Without strong leadership, the campaign is likely to fizzle out within months.

items.question:
Choose the correct phrasal verb:
The city is about to ___ an ambitious ten-year plan to modernise public transport.
items.explanation: “embark on” = to start something new, important or difficult. Full sentence: The city is about to embark on an ambitious ten-year plan to modernise public transport.

items.question:
Choose the correct phrasal verb:
Many believe artificial intelligence will ___ a new era in medicine.
items.explanation: “usher in” = to mark or cause the start of a new period. Full sentence: Many believe artificial intelligence will usher in a new era in medicine.

items.question:
Choose the correct phrasal verb:
He has an irritating habit of trying to ___ whenever two people are talking.
items.explanation: “butt in” = to interrupt a conversation rudely. Full sentence: He has an irritating habit of trying to butt in whenever two people are talking.

items.question:
Choose the correct phrasal verb:
Try not to ___ the negative comments; most of the feedback was positive.
items.meaningVi: day dứt, cứ nghĩ mãi về
items.explanation: “dwell on” = to keep thinking or talking about something unpleasant. Full sentence: Try not to dwell on the negative comments; most of the feedback was positive.

items.question:
Choose the correct phrasal verb:
Unexpected costs always seem to ___ when you renovate an old house.
items.explanation: “crop up” = to happen or appear unexpectedly. Full sentence: Unexpected costs always seem to crop up when you renovate an old house.

items.question:
Choose the correct phrasal verb:
The new software helps banks ___ fraudulent transactions.
items.explanation: “weed out” = to remove unwanted people or things from a group. Full sentence: The new software helps banks weed out fraudulent transactions.

items.question:
Choose the correct phrasal verb:
Farmers are beginning to ___ for the harvest.
items.explanation: “gear up” = to prepare for something that is going to happen. Full sentence: Farmers are beginning to gear up for the harvest.

items.question:
Choose the correct phrasal verb:
Whether the match goes ahead will ___ the condition of the pitch.
items.explanation: “hinge on” = to depend completely on something. Full sentence: Whether the match goes ahead will hinge on the condition of the pitch.

items.question:
Choose the correct phrasal verb:
By signing the contract, you agree to ___ the terms and conditions.
items.explanation: “abide by” = to accept and obey a rule, law or decision. Full sentence: By signing the contract, you agree to abide by the terms and conditions.

items.question:
Choose the correct phrasal verb:
When people feel humiliated, they sometimes ___ at those closest to them.
items.meaningVi: đả kích, nổi xung tấn công
items.explanation: “lash out” = to suddenly attack or criticise someone angrily. Full sentence: When people feel humiliated, they sometimes lash out at those closest to them.

items.question:
Choose the correct phrasal verb:
The film was so slow that I started to ___ halfway through.
items.explanation: “nod off” = to fall asleep, especially when you do not intend to. Full sentence: The film was so slow that I started to nod off halfway through.

items.question:
Choose the correct phrasal verb:
Fans were furious at having to ___ nearly £100 for a concert ticket.
items.explanation: “fork out” = to spend a lot of money on something, often unwillingly. Full sentence: Fans were furious at having to fork out nearly £100 for a concert ticket.
